# Deal aging / WIP report

Which open deals are stalled — how long each deal has sat in its current stage, each stage's average age, and exactly which deals are aging well past their peers.

Family: Value stream mapping · Format: .xlsx · Domain: commercial

## What it is

A stalled deal sitting in a pipeline stage is work-in-process the same way an unfinished part sitting in a queue is — capital tied up, risk accumulating, and a signal something's blocking it specifically. This tool measures one thing per open deal: how many days it's been in its current stage. From that it computes each stage's average age and names which deals are aging at least twice their stage's average — those are stalled, not just aging normally through a slower stage.

## When to use it

Use it when:

- You can pull real per-deal stage-entry dates from the CRM for every currently-open deal in a bounded segment.
- You want to know which specific deals need a check-in now, not just an overall sense that the pipeline feels slow.
- You suspect a small number of deals are stuck and skewing how the pipeline looks in a snapshot review.

Not when:

- You want completed-deal cycle time, not currently-open deals — that's the sales funnel value stream map.
- You only have a pipeline value total with no per-deal stage-entry dates — there's nothing to compute an age from.
- The pipeline segment blends deal types with genuinely different natural stage durations — scope down to one comparable segment first, same discipline as every other VSM-family artifact.

## How to fill it in

- **scope** — Which deal source or segment, as of what date? Keep it to one comparable segment — a blended pipeline produces stage averages that describe neither.
- **items** — List every currently-open deal with its current stage and the date it entered that stage. Pull real dates from CRM stage-history, not a gut-sense estimate of how long a deal has felt stuck.
- **stages** — Each stage's average age among its currently-open deals — computed for you, nothing to enter here.
- **summary** — The overall average age, the single oldest open deal, and which deals are flagged as stalled (aging at least twice their stage's average) — all computed for you.
- **narrative** — Drafted from the stall flags and your observation notes — what the rep or RevOps has actually seen about why a specific deal is stuck.
- **countermeasures** — What will you do about the stalled deals, ranked by impact and effort, owned and dated? A countermeasure not tied to a named stalled deal is a coaching failure mode, not a real action.

## What good looks like

The example below is an outbound mid-market pipeline's deal aging: real stage-entry dates per deal, stage averages with the arithmetic shown, one deal correctly flagged as stalled at more than 2x its stage's average, and a countermeasure that traces directly to that specific deal rather than a generic 'work the pipeline harder' push.

Full worked example, on-screen and as a downloadable .xlsx: https://katafacts.com/katas/deal-aging-report

## Common mistakes

- **Treating every open deal with a nonzero age as worth a check-in.** — Same vital-few discipline as the rest of this catalogue — one deal genuinely stalled relative to its stage-mates beats a list of every deal that isn't brand new.
- **Comparing a deal's age against the overall pipeline average instead of its own stage's average.** — A naturally slower stage (negotiation vs. a quick discovery call, say) will always look 'stalled' against the overall average even when every deal in it is moving normally — the comparison has to be within the stage.
- **Estimating stage-entry dates from memory instead of pulling real CRM stage-history.** — Reps' recall skews toward memorable deals, not typical ones — the CRM's actual stage-transition timestamps are the ground truth here, same as every other data-driven artifact in this catalogue.

## What it connects to

Upstream:

- **Sales funnel value stream map** — The same stage-level thinking, applied to completed deals instead of currently-open ones — useful together when a stage is both slow on average and producing stalled outliers.

Downstream:

- **Deal A3** — Once a stalled deal is named, a deal A3 is where you'd run root cause analysis on why that specific deal is stuck, if it isn't already obvious from the observation notes.

## Where AI helps

Judgement — stays with you:

- Deciding whether a stalled deal needs immediate rep escalation or can wait for the next pipeline review
- Committing to which countermeasure to act on first

Analysis — AI helps:

- Drafting the narrative from rep/RevOps observation notes and the stall-flag findings
- Pressure-testing whether a proposed countermeasure actually addresses the named stalled deal

Drudgery — automated:

- Computing every deal's age, each stage's average, and which deals are stalled, with the arithmetic shown
- Identifying the single oldest open deal in the pipeline
- Exporting to xlsx in the house format
